result:
I planned round 331 as stage c2a of the drag-preview performance work. B's decision is CONTINUE, and `store/` is untouched (0 entries in `git status`).

**Round 330 result.** C passed round 330 with real browser checks, 11/11 rows and no bugs. Gate 330 published both rounds 329 and 330 as `1e5f552`. Stage c1 is done, and C-R329-01, C-R329-02 and C-R328-01 are closed in the backlog on that evidence. The round-330 task is archived as a byte-equal copy in `tasks/round-330.md`. Regression is due only for rounds planned on or after 2026-11-05, so the next round is a feature stage.

**Round 331 task.** While a clip's fade is dragged, the selected-clip readout and the detail panel stop re-rendering, because they show no fade or envelope field. During a same-lane move, the readout no longer looks up the clip while the lane-move hint replaces it. A applies a patch I already tested, `b-round-330/sketch/sketch.patch.txt`, plus one doc update (doc 232). That makes 5 files; the detail panel itself, the protected files and `perf/` stay untouched.

The field list must name every clip field, so a new field fails to compile until someone decides whether it is shown. A test (DP27) compares a fresh render of a clip against one that differs only in an ignored field, so a later change that starts showing a fade without updating the list goes red.

**Measured on the sketch** (production build, run alone, compared with C round 330):

| Drag | Components per move before | After | Max before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fade | 21.633 | 13.767 | 22 → 14 |
| Move | 30.367 | 29.4 | 108 → 107 |
| Trim | unchanged | unchanged | — |

- 104 other perf rows are equal and all 36 asserted rows pass; the browser render probe agrees with these numbers.
- Full vitest passes 3570/3570, and all 7 mutants go red on their target tests.
- Testing caught two mistakes in my own plan before dispatch: the readout does not legitimately render during a move (the hint replaces it), and my first version of DP27 could not fail.

**C will check** that the change lists exactly 5 files, then run the unit tests three times, the mutants, the browser render counts and the perf spec. In the browser, at 1440×900 and 1280×720, C compares A against HEAD on fade, trim, the move hint and a two-clip group gain change. C also checks that the export file is byte-identical to HEAD and that `/studio-lab` still opens without sign-in while purchased Studio stays protected.

**How I resolved the consult disagreement** (both read-only):
- **Overview:** performance-optimizer wanted it in this round, tech-lead wanted it held because its code keeps changing and a frontend-architect checkpoint is pending. I followed tech-lead; the overview moves to c2b, where it goes ahead whether or not the checkpoint has been answered by then.
- **Narrowing the clip type to the shown fields (`Pick`):** tech-lead preferred this. I rejected it because it would spread into shared lane code; it stays as a signal for the later micro-fades work.
- **Two smaller items:** gate-330's two doc Lows are fixed in this round, and its architecture proposal is recorded as a signal, not scheduled.

**One acceptance row rests on a recipe I did not run:** the two-clip group row (Shift+click a second clip). It comes from the code and is marked as a deviation from the claims rule (L29). If C can't reach the group view at HEAD, that is not a failure of A.

The configured advisor was available and I used it three times; it shaped the c2a/c2b split, the stale-display test and the perf row wording.

**Next:** round 332 is REGRESSION if planned on or after 2026-11-05, otherwise stage c2b. After that come c3–c5, PERF-9…15, STEM-LANES, SYS-1…3 and STORE-2b…5. Saba-gated items remain parked as before. My scratch copy is `/home/runner/b330-scratch`, and the dev server I started is stopped.
